questions.prompt: A 3840×2160 image is processed with 32×8 blocks. How many threads are launched in total?
A block of 24×5 threads. How many warps, and how many idle lanes? Answer with the number of idle lanes.
In blocks of 256, which condition never causes divergence?
options: if (threadIdx.x % 32 < 16)
if ((threadIdx.x >> 5) & 1)
if (threadIdx.x == 0)
if (data[i] > 0)
questions.explanation: (threadIdx.x >> 5) is the warp number; its low bit is constant within a warp.

questions.prompt: Half a warp takes a 12-instruction path and the other half an 8-instruction path. SIMD efficiency of that if/else, in percent?
A 3×3 filter must handle image borders. Which approach keeps interior warps free of divergence?
options: if (x == 0 || y == 0 || …) { special case } else { normal }
Clamp each neighbour coordinate with min/max
Skip border pixels with continue
Use a separate kernel per pixel
questions.explanation: Clamping is branch-free, so no warp diverges because of borders.

questions.prompt: Which are true about the 2008 Tesla architecture paper?
options: It introduced the term SIMT and warps of 32 threads
Each SM could keep hundreds of threads resident
It used separate vertex and pixel processors
It made graphics and general computing share one array of processors
questions.explanation: Unification replaced separate vertex and pixel processors.

questions.prompt: Why can't dynamic warp formation freely move a thread to any lane?
options: Lanes have different instruction sets
Its registers live in its home lane's register-file bank
Memory addresses are per lane
The scheduler forbids it
questions.explanation: The register file is banked by lane, so regrouping is lane-aware.
